clue.text: Act as Bond, Connery-style?

indicators.note: Sean Connery famously slurs his S sounds into SH, so the S of the word is said his way

parts.note: to bond is to adhere, as glue makes things stick

explanation.surface: A question about whether to play 007 the way Sean Connery did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Connery-style' swaps the opening S of STICK for SH, mimicking Sean Connery's lisping S, the first actor to play James Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtick is a performer's habitual routine or comic gimmick, their act.

clue.text: In on

explanation.definitionFit: Something trendy is described as a lively, current scene, and an event that is occurring is under way right now.

clue.text: I live by narrow inlet somewhere in Europe

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a ria is a long narrow sea inlet formed by a drowned river valley

explanation.surface: Someone says they live beside a narrow creek somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula holding Spain and Portugal is a region of south-west Europe.

clue.text: One captures Farage fan getting in with revolutionary

indicators.note: getting in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Nigel Farage led UKIP, whose supporters were nicknamed kippers

indicators.note: revolutionary turns the short linking word around

parts.note: with means and, joining things together

explanation.surface: A supporter of Farage teams up with a revolutionary to take someone captive.
explanation.walkthrough: UKIP was a British anti-EU party led by Nigel Farage, and its supporters were nicknamed kippers. 'Revolutionary' reverses the word given by 'with', and 'getting in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper is a person who seizes and holds someone, one who captures.

clue.text: On which 747 is sir given important place to sleep?

parts.note: key means crucial or important
a pad is slang for a flat or a place to crash

explanation.surface: An aviation riddle: where on a jumbo jet does a knighted passenger get a prominent berth?
explanation.walkthrough: 747 suggests a Boeing jumbo, but on a phone's buttons 7 carries PQRS and 4 carries GHI, so typing 7-4-7 can spell SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: On a phone's number buttons each digit stands for letters, so the digits 7, 4, 7 can spell out the word sir.

clue.text: Course on leaving it tidy

indicators.note: leaving says the following letters depart from the word

parts.note: Kempton Park is a racecourse near London

explanation.surface: A golf or racing instruction to leave the course neat.
explanation.walkthrough: Kempton Park is a horse-racing course in Surrey; removing ON from KEMPTON leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kempt, the rarely used positive of unkempt, means neatly kept, especially of hair.

clue.text: Most horrible keys I cut in error

indicators.note: in error means wrongly made, so the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they cut the wrong keys, a dreadful outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Yucky is informal for disgusting, so its superlative means the most disgusting.

clue.text: Single bananas I declined to bag

indicators.note: to bag is to capture and hold, so the answer is held inside the words before

explanation.surface: Someone turned down a lone banana rather than put it in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' tempts as an anagram signal, but nothing is rearranged: the letters sit inside bananAS I DEclined.
explanation.definitionFit: On a vinyl single the featured track sits on the main side, so the release is named after it.

clue.text: One who's not shocked left out idiot

indicators.note: out tells us a letter is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: someone with no shock of hair is bald, and British slang for a bald man is slaphead

explanation.surface: Someone who stayed calm after a fright is dismissed as a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not shocked' reads as unsurprised, but it means having no shock of hair. SLAPHEAD is British slang for a bald man; dropping L leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A saphead is a dated word for a simpleton or fool.

clue.text: They reject religion, as its rules start to cause riots

indicators.note: the rules run riot, so their letters are thrown into disorder
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Atheists push back against faith because its rules provoke rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riots' looks like the end of the story but signals the anagram of AS ITS RULES with C ('start to cause').
explanation.definitionFit: Secularists argue that public life should be kept free of religious influence.

clue.text: When there's a loud boom, I must replace old device

indicators.note: must replace says one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: a sonic boom happens at Mach one, the speed of sound

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap out an old gadget once it starts making a loud bang.
explanation.walkthrough: MACH ONE (the speed of sound, where a sonic boom occurs) has its O (old) replaced by I.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine is a mechanical apparatus, a synonym for a device.

clue.text: Old country festival loads get to begin entering

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: to begin points to the opening letter

parts.note: loads means a great many

explanation.surface: A historic nation's festival in which crowds start to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to begin' gives G, which 'entering' places inside EASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The German Democratic Republic existed from 1949 to 1990, a nation that no longer exists.

clue.text: More than one can camp to go on

definitions.text: More than one can camp to go on

parts.words: More than one can camp to go on
parts.note: a can is slang for a lavatory, and these portable ones are used on campsites; 'to go' hints at going to the loo

explanation.surface: Seems to say several people can go camping together.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'can' as a noun, slang for a lavatory: several camp toilets you sit on to 'go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable lavatories that use chemicals rather than drains are standard camping equipment, plural here.

clue.text: Lane possibly leads to lake, one in Surrey

indicators.note: the leads of the next words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Directions: a country lane runs down to a lake in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lane' looks like a road but is the surname of Superman's colleague Lois Lane; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lois Lane is the reporter in Superman stories, so she is one person named Lane.

clue.text: Work records what bully's doing?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a vinyl record is a pressing, made by pressing it from a master

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style question about what a thug is up to, after mentioning work records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work records' looks like employment files, but it is OP (opus) plus PRESSING, a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: A bully is engaged in tyrannising or crushing others, so the participle describes the bully's activity.

clue.text: Dodgy clue time! Shout about it being unenthusiastic

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other pieces

parts.note: to rant is to shout angrily

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver complains about a dodgy clue, unwilling to engage with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy clue' reads as a solver's grumble but is the anagram; 'about' wraps the shout around the mixed letters plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reluctant means unwilling or hesitant, lacking any eagerness.

clue.text: Been? I went dancing neither before nor after

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone asked where they were explains they went out dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in the middle comes neither first nor last, but in the gap between.

clue.text: Rapper detailed new intros to copyright every note

indicators.note: detailed means losing the tail, the final letter

parts.note: Eminem is a famous American rapper

indicators.note: intros are the openings, so take the first letters

explanation.surface: A rap star with new music claims copyright on every note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks musical, but it means distinction, as in 'a person of note'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of note has distinction and high standing, which is prominence.

clue.text: Process to fix a part for mother?

parts.note: to rig is to fix a result dishonestly
ma is an informal word for mother
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Asks how to sort out a part in the play for Mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tiresome procedure, a drawn-out process.

clue.text: Tower on slope — start climb via door at the rear

indicators.note: the rear of each word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Mountaineering advice: begin the ascent by going out through the back door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like an instruction, but it is the first of four words whose last letters are taken; 'Tower' is something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift with T-shaped bars drags skiers up the piste, so it is a thing that tows on a slope.

clue.text: Unravel crossword in which there's something to get stuck on

indicators.note: in which there's says the answer sits inside the words before

explanation.surface: Solving a crossword where there is a clue you get stuck on.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting stuck on a crossword is the surface; the answer sits within unraVEL CROssword.
explanation.definitionFit: The hook-and-loop fastener sticks two surfaces together, so things get stuck on it.

clue.text: Those bowing to rich strangers post acrobatics

indicators.note: after a bout of acrobatics the letters of the words before are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Performers take a bow to wealthy strangers after an acrobatic display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowing' suggests taking a bow; it means playing with a bow. 'Post acrobatics' (after acrobatics) rearranges TO RICH STRANGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Violinists, violists and cellists draw bows across strings, so an ensemble of them is made of players who bow.

clue.text: An American's observation of cheat, not for the first time

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to con is to cheat or swindle

explanation.surface: An American spots a cheat who has done it before.
explanation.walkthrough: Recon is a US short form of reconnaissance, hence 'An American's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recon is US military slang for reconnaissance, a scouting or surveying mission.

clue.text: Start both notes off — and tones

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician starts both sets of notes off, followed by tones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both' means two fodders work: NOTES mixed up ('off') gives the answer, and so does TONES; the parse shows one.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, the point where it starts.

clue.text: One hand indicates this, another helping

definitions.meaning: a clock's thinnest, fastest hand counts off these small units of time
going back for more food at a meal

explanation.surface: A clock's hand points the way while someone takes more food.
explanation.definitionFit: The second hand of a clock shows elapsed seconds, and seconds are also a further serving of food.

clue.text: Sport that woman needs bow to start, close to body?

indicators.note: to start puts this piece at the front of what follows

parts.note: a bow is curved, an arc
her refers to a woman

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Suggests a woman must bow to begin, near to her body, as in a ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: The bow is also the archer's weapon, so the clue nearly describes the sport itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting arrows at a target with a bow is an Olympic sport.

clue.text: Batting order for cricket?

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a religious order is a sect

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about the batting order in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' is the chirping creature, not the game; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket is a chirping bug, one example of the six-legged creatures.

clue.text: Difficult defendant finally up for it

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: up for it is slang for sexually eager

explanation.surface: A tricky defendant who is, in the end, keen to get on with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is one full of difficulties, as a bramble is full of prickles.
